source: Bush, R. 2010. 'Large Ruminant Nutrition Theory, Part 2: Silages and Better Feeding Practices', University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com), including a Village Livestock Agent (VLA) fattening-cattle feeding trial conducted in Tbong Khmum, Aug-Dec 2009. Same font/ligature encoding quirk as Source O, decoded the same way.
text: Silage is recommended as a way to store surplus forage cut during the growing season for use fattening animals in the dry season, since animals need to receive at least 15% of their body weight in feed every day to fatten properly, and this is hard to sustain from fresh-cut forage alone through the dry season. Production: dig a pit 1.5-2.0m deep; chop young grass into 4-6cm lengths (older grass 1-3cm) and compact it into 30-40cm layers; keep air out of the finished pit with a thorough soil covering, since silage fermentation passes through an aerobic phase, a lag phase, a fermentation phase, a stable phase, and finally a feed-out phase, and oxygen exposure at the wrong stage spoils the silage.
